answer: A strong defence is stake-backed reputation that grows only through a long voyage of verifiable work: each agent locks collateral and earns trust slowly by completing attested tasks, so a fresh identity starts at the inlet with almost no voting or reward power. An attacker who wants many influential fakes must therefore pay the stake and the time cost for every single one, while an umber flag on sudden bursts of new identities lets the network throttle them before they can sway anything.
